heading: Idle Persons.

items.text: Work diligently at your calling and spend honestly, so that your household does not come to want or need relief from others.
items.citation: General Laws and Liberties, Idle Persons
items.quote: that have Families to provide for, who greatly neglect their Callings, or mispend what they earn, whereby their Families are in much want

work: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printe
heading: FORNICATION.

items.text: Maintain and bring up the child born of fornication.
items.quote: he shall be at the care and charge to maintain and bring up the same

items.text: Assist in the care and upbringing of a child born of fornication as natural duty requires.
items.quote: by such Assistance of the Mother as nature requireth

work: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printe
heading: DOWRIES.

items.text: Assign to the widow her just third part, with conveniency or to her satisfaction, within one month after lawful demand.
items.citation: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, DOWRIES
items.quote: shall not within one Month after lawful demand made, assigne and set out to such Widdow her just third part
items.needs_role: Heir of the husband or other person interested

items.text: Do not strip or waste the dower lands; maintain the houses, fences and enclosures, and leave them in good repair.
items.citation: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, DOWRIES
items.quote: shall not commit or suffer any strip or waste, but shall maintain all such Houses, Fences and Inclosures
items.needs_role: Heir or person entitled to the reversion

work: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printe
heading: Age for plaintiffs and Defendants.

items.text: Plead and defend in civil cases for your children under twenty-one, as you see meet.
items.citation: Massachusetts Laws, Age for plaintiffs and Defendants.
items.quote: for all persons under that age, their Parents, Masters, and Guardians as they shall see meet shall plead and defend their right and interest

items.text: Plead and defend in civil cases for your ward under twenty-one, as you see meet.
items.citation: Massachusetts Laws, Age for plaintiffs and Defendants.
items.quote: for all persons under that age, their Parents, Masters, and Guardians as they shall see meet shall plead and defend their right and interest

items.text: Plead and defend in civil cases for your servants under twenty-one, as you see meet.
items.citation: Massachusetts Laws, Age for plaintiffs and Defendants.
items.quote: for all persons under that age, their Parents, Masters, and Guardians as they shall see meet shall plead and defend their right and interest

work: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printe
heading: Marriages and Married Persons. … Sect. 5

items.text: Do not strike her.
items.citation: Massachusetts Laws, Marriages and Married Persons, 1
items.quote: no man shall strike his Wife

items.text: Do not strike him.
items.citation: Massachusetts Laws, Marriages and Married Persons, 1
items.quote: nor any Woman her Husband

items.text: Seek to win a young woman's affection only after obtaining her parents' consent; do not visit her secretly.
items.citation: Massachusetts Laws, Marriages and Married Persons, 3
items.quote: to draw away the Affection of any Maid in this Jurisdiction, under pretence of Marriage, before he hath obtained liberty and allowance from her Parents

items.text: If your spouse is overseas, repair to them at the first opportunity.
items.citation: Massachusetts Laws, Marriages and Married Persons, 4
items.quote: all such married persons as aforesaid, shall repair to their said Relations by the first opportunity of shipping

items.text: Do not marry your deceased wife's sister.
items.citation: Massachusetts Laws, Marriages and Married Persons, Answer (1679)
items.quote: The Court resolves it en the Negative.
items.conflict: Prohibition of marriage with a deceased wife's sister is not in Scripture; many Reformed churches allow it.

work: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printe
heading: SCHOOLS. … Sect. 3

items.text: Pay the wages of the schoolmaster who teaches your child to read and write, that they may gain knowledge of the Scriptures.
items.quote: whose Wages shall be paid either by the Parents or Masters of such Children

items.text: Pay the wages of the schoolmaster who teaches the children in your charge to read and write.
items.quote: whose Wages shall be paid either by the Parents or Masters of such Children

work: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printe
heading: CAPITAL LAWS. … Sect. 17

items.text: Do not curse or smite your natural father or mother.
items.quote: shall CURSE or SMITE their natural FATHER or MOTHER

items.text: Obey your father and mother; do not be stubborn or rebellious.
items.quote: will not obey the voice of his Father, or the voice of his Mother

items.text: Correct and discipline your children so that they may learn obedience.
items.quote: when they had chastened him, will not hearken unto them

items.text: Do not provoke your children by extreme and cruel correction; educate them faithfully.
items.quote: the Parents have been very unchristianly negligent in the education of such Children, or so provoked them by extreme and cruel Correction

items.text: Be faithful to your spouse; do not commit adultery with a married or espoused person.
items.quote: If any Person COMMIT ADULTERY with a Married or Espoused Wife, the Adulterer and the Adulteress shall surely be put to death

items.text: Do not commit carnal copulation with a child under ten years old; it is heinous and harmful.
items.quote: Carnal Copulation with a Woman Childe, under the age of ten years, is a more hainous sin

work: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printe
heading: Children and Youth. · Sect. 6

items.text: Do not dispose of an orphan during minority without the consent of a court.
items.citation: Massachusetts Laws, Children and Youth Sect. 6
items.quote: No Orphan ... shall afterwards be absolutely disposed of by any, withont the consent of some Court

items.text: Do not permit a female orphan under sixteen to marry without the consent of the town selectmen or an assistant.
items.citation: Massachusetts Laws, Children and Youth Sect. 6
items.quote: in case of marriage ... approbation of the major part of the Select men ... shall be sufficient, and the minority of women ... sixteen yeares.

work: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printe
heading: WILLS. … Sect. 3

items.text: Prove and record the will of a deceased kinsman, or take administration of his estate, within the month after his death, before possessing or disposing of any of his goods.
items.quote: if any person whatsoever, shall not within the same time take Administration of all such Goods, as he hath or shall enter upon of any Party deceased

items.text: If a kinsman dies intestate, seek administration of his estate so that the court may appoint someone; do not leave it to the town clerk to report.
items.quote: if none of the friends or kindred of the deceased party that shall dy intestate, shall seek for Administration... then the Clerke... shall give notice

work: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printe
heading: Masters, Servants, Labourers. … Sect. 9

items.text: Do not give, sell or barter any commodity without your master's license during your service.
items.quote: That no servant either Man or Maid, shall either give, sell or truck any Commodity whatsoever without License from their Masters

items.text: Work the whole day, allowing convenient time for food and rest.
items.quote: all Workmen, shall work the whole day, allowing convenient time for food and rest.

items.text: Do not run away from your master; if you flee, you will be pursued and brought back.
items.quote: when any Servants shall run from their Masters, or any other Inhabitants shall privily go away with suspition of civil intentions

items.text: Pay your servant or workman wages; you may pay in corn valued by two indifferent men.
items.quote: they may be paid in Corn, to be valued by two indifferent Freemen

items.text: Do not assign your servant to another for more than a year without consent of the court or two assistants.
items.quote: no servant shall be put off for above a year to any other... unless it be by consent of Authority assembled in some Court, or two Assistants

items.text: If you smite out your servant's eye or tooth, or otherwise maim or disfigure them, let them go free and allow further recompense.
items.quote: if any man smite out the Eye or Tooth of his Man-servant or Maid servant, or otherwise maim or much disfigure them... he shall let them go free from his service, and shall allow such further Recompence

items.text: After seven years of diligent service, do not send your servant away empty; give them a benefit.
items.quote: all servants that have served diligently and faithfully, to the benefit of their Masters, Seven years, shall not be sent away empty

items.text: If you have been unfaithful, negligent or unprofitable, make satisfaction before dismissal.
items.quote: if any have been unfaithful, negligent or unprofitable in their service... they shall not be dismissed, till they have made satisfaction according to the judgement of Authority

work: The General Laws and Liberties of the Massachusets Colony, revised and re-printe
heading: Children and Youth. … Sect. 5

items.text: Teach your children to read the English tongue and to know the capital laws.
items.quote: teach, by themselves or others, their Children and Apprentices, so much learning, as may enable them perfectly to read the English tongue, and knowledge of the Capital Lawes

items.text: Teach your servants and apprentices to read the English tongue and to know the capital laws.
items.quote: teach, by themselves or others, their Children and Apprentices, so much learning, as may enable them perfectly to read the English tongue, and knowledge of the Capital Lawes

items.text: Catechize your children weekly in the grounds and principles of religion.
items.quote: all Masters of families, do once a week (at the least) Catechise their children and servants in the Grounds and Principles of Religion

items.text: Catechize your servants weekly in the grounds and principles of religion.
items.quote: all Masters of families, do once a week (at the least) Catechise their children and servants in the Grounds and Principles of Religion

items.text: Bring up your children in some honest lawful calling or employment.
items.quote: breed and bring up their chilren and apprentices in some honest lawfull Calling, Labour or imployment

items.text: Bring up your servants and apprentices in some honest lawful calling or employment.
items.quote: breed and bring up their chilren and apprentices in some honest lawfull Calling, Labour or imployment

items.text: Obey your parents and governors; do not be disobedient or disorderly toward them.
items.quote: do behave themselves disobediently and disorderly towards their Parents, Masters and Governours

items.text: Obey your master; do not be disobedient or disorderly toward him.
items.quote: do behave themselves disobediently and disorderly towards their Parents, Masters and Governours

items.text: Do not entertain children or servants under another's government; discharge them to their callings and lodgings.
items.quote: cause or suffer any Young people... to spend any of their time or estate... and shall not... discharge and hasten all such Youths to their several imployments

items.text: Do not willfully and unreasonably deny your child timely or convenient marriage.
items.quote: shall willfully and unreasonably deny any Child, timely or convenient marriage

items.text: Do not exercise any unnatural severity toward your children.
items.quote: shall excercise any unnatural severity toward them
